name: Interval Integration for Volumetric Light Scattering
definition: A method to compute in-scattered radiance by decomposing the integration path into intervals defined by front and back faces of a light volume, allowing analytical evaluation of the scattering integral for directional lights and numerical or lookup-based evaluation for point/spot lights.
summary: Interval Integration computes in-scattered radiance by decomposing ray paths into intervals defined by light volume boundaries, enabling a sum-and-difference approach that sets it apart from sibling methods.
